Leaves appear slightly curled. This suggests either Powdery Mildew (white powdery coating on stems) or possibly Bacterial Canker (stem lesions with white spots).

Let me view reference images across 8 different classes, starting with the most likely candidates.

Very interesting! This Bacterial Canker reference (ID 5606081) shows stem exudate/white deposits - the IDs 5606081 and 5606088 (test image) are very close, suggesting same photo series. Let me check a few more classes.

I've now viewed 9 reference images across 7 classes. Based on my analysis:

**Key observations from test image (Bugwood 5606088):**
- Tomato stem with white/granular deposits scattered along the surface
- Stem otherwise appears green and healthy
- Slightly curled/distorted leaves

**Reference comparison:**
- **Bacterial Canker (Bugwood_18.jpg, ID 5606081)**: Right panel shows white/cream deposits on stem exterior -- very similar pattern. IDs 5606081, 5606085, and 5606088 are from the same Bugwood series, strongly suggesting the same disease
- **Powdery Mildew**: Showed white circular patches on leaves, not stem deposits
- **Bacterial Speck**: Dark spots on leaves, not matching
- **Alternaria**: Dark/black stem necrosis, not matching
- **Early Blight**: Yellow-brown leaf necrosis, not matching
- **Sclerotinia**: Whole plant collapse, not matching

The white exudate/deposits on the hairy tomato stem in the test image most closely match the bacterial canker stem symptoms visible in the reference images from the same photographic series.
